notes: Bandwidth figures are approximate (dual-channel DDR4-3200 and 192-bit GDDR6) and should be verified.

name: Custom Build Desktop
notes: Motherboard: TRX40 Designare. RAM reports 2133 MT/s. The 68 GB/s figure assumes all 4 memory channels are populated at that speed, and the GPU figure assumes a 352-bit bus at 14 Gbps. Both are approximate and should be verified. If 2133 MT/s is the default speed rather than the rated speed, enabling XMP/DOCP in the BIOS would raise CPU-offload speeds.

name: Beelink Mini S12 Pro
gpu: Intel UHD Graphics (integrated, shares system RAM)
notes: No dedicated GPU, so models run on the CPU. The 25.6 GB/s figure assumes single-channel DDR4-3200 (the N100's limit) and should be verified. The integrated GPU is not counted: Ollama does not use Intel integrated graphics by default. With only 4 cores, real speeds may be lower than the bandwidth estimate and long prompts will be slow to start.

name: ZimaBlade 3760
gpu: Intel HD Graphics (integrated, shares system RAM)
notes: No usable GPU, so models run on the CPU. One SODIMM slot with DDR3L-1333 gives roughly 10.7 GB/s (single channel, approximate: verify). Only 2 cores, and as far as I know this CPU lacks the AVX instructions llama.cpp uses for speed, so real speeds will likely be lower than the estimates. Assumes a lightweight Linux install, so 2 GB is kept free for the OS.

name: MacBook Air M2 (24 GB)
cpu: Apple M2 (8-core CPU, 10-core GPU, 16-core Neural Engine)
notes: CPU and GPU share the 24 GB of unified memory. The 100 GB/s figure is Apple's published M2 memory bandwidth (verify). The page lets the GPU use about 70% of RAM because macOS limits GPU memory by default; that limit can be raised in system settings, but leave room for macOS. Fanless design, so long runs may throttle.

name: Raspberry Pi Model B (original)
cpu: Broadcom BCM2835 ARM11 (single core, 700 MHz, 32-bit ARMv6)
no_ollama_note: This board has 512 MB of RAM and a 32-bit ARMv6 CPU. As far as I know Ollama only ships for 64-bit systems, so it will not install here, and no chat model in this list fits in 512 MB anyway. At most a tiny embedding model could fit in memory, and you would have to build the runtime yourself. Realistically this board is not a host for local AI: use it for other jobs, or point tools running on it at Ollama on one of your other machines.
notes: Original Raspberry Pi Model B with 512 MB RAM (rev 2). The 1 GB/s memory bandwidth is a very rough guess: verify. Fit labels in the table below only compare model size to memory and ignore the Ollama limitation.

name: Pixel 9a (phone)
gpu: Arm Mali GPU (not used by most phone apps)
notes: Phone with 8 GB of RAM and a Google Tensor G4 chip (Google's spec; storage is 128 or 256 GB, check yours). It runs models in an app such as PocketPal AI, not with Ollama. The 3.5 GB kept free for Android and your other apps, and the 51 GB/s memory speed, are rough guesses: verify them. Phones slow down when hot, and Android can close an app that uses too much memory, so choose models well under the limit. Use the app's Benchmark page to measure real speed, then record it as 'measured' (see calibration.md).
